source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1d; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 + private pension (person 0) 30,000.00 + Railroad Retirement (person 0) 40,000.00 = 110,000.00. Federal taxable income = 110,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 92,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 110,000.00. Schedule M line 1d Railroad Retirement 40,000.00 (exempt in full, no age or income test). Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70): yes; question 2 federal AGI 110,000.00 less than or equal to 107,000.00: no. Not both yes: no table, modification 0.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 40,000.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 40,000.00 = -40,000.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -40,000.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 110,000.00 + (-40,000.00) = 70,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 70,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 70,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 59,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 59,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 54,000.00. Line 8 tax on 54,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 54,000.00 x 0.0375 = 2025.000000 = 2,025.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 2,025.00. Note: Federal AGI 110,000 fails question 2 even though line 3 would be under 107,000: the income test reads federal AGI, before the railroad subtraction. Railroad Retirement stays exempt.
